docs.title: v0.2.0 status
docs.text:
This documentation describes the locally implemented v0.2.0 candidate. Publication and hosted GitHub Actions acceptance remain pending. Install the checkout or a locally built wheel to use these changes before publication.

The main purpose is consistent evaluation across CLI, Python, pytest, and CI: explicit baseline selection, per-question quality gates, comparable reports, and reliable automation output. See the release and migration guide and verification record.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
"Did my last commit break retrieval?" — now you know in seconds.

LongProbe is a sub-second RAG regression harness. Define your Golden Questions once, run longprobe check on every commit, and get an exact diff of which document chunks were lost in your latest change — before your users notice.

Think pytest --watch for your RAG pipeline.

docs.title: Why LongProbe?
docs.text:
Every RAG developer faces the same silent killer: you refactor chunking strategy, upgrade LangChain, or add a new document — and your retrieval silently degrades. DeepEval and RAGChecker are heavyweight evaluation frameworks meant for batch analysis, not fast regression checks in a dev loop.

LongProbe gives you instant feedback:

  • ⚡ Sub-second checks on small golden sets
  • 🔍 Exact diffs showing which chunks were lost/gained
  • 📊 Recall scores with per-question breakdown
  • 💾 Baseline tracking to catch regressions over time
  • 🧪 pytest integration for existing test suites
  • 🔌 Pluggable adapters for any vector store

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
The package-index command below installs the published version. For the unreleased candidate, follow checkout installation. Configure a working retriever and review golden evidence before saving a baseline.

# Install
pip install longprobe

# Initialize
longprobe init

# Define your golden questions in goldens.yaml
# Configure your vector store in longprobe.yaml

# Run checks
longprobe check

# Save baseline
longprobe baseline save --label v1.0

# Compare after changes
longprobe diff --baseline v1.0

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Versioned evaluation contracts and shared JSON/SQLite report validation; legacy rows remain readable without automatic rewriting.
  • Explicit per-question thresholds, baseline quality policy, reference identity, and coverage/requirement/evidence differences.
  • check --baseline LABEL, check --no-compare, JSON baseline-save output, and read-only report PATH rendering.
  • Supported session-scoped longprobe_report pytest fixture and automatic opt-in quality enforcement.
  • Trusted baseline artifact restoration and one-evaluation CI feedback with retained diagnostics.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• CLI and Python share evaluation and baseline promotion; the default requires every evaluated approved question to pass.
  • Equal-recall loss of required evidence is a regression. Changed contracts/coverage and metadata-free references cannot certify strict comparison.
  • Parsed JSON commands emit one stdout document; handled failures use safe error envelopes and documented exit categories.
  • Reusable CI honors package version selection and only relaxes completed quality failures when explicitly configured.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
• Back up old baseline databases and explicitly establish reviewed new-format references; no SQL table migration is required.
  • Global threshold overrides preserve explicit per-question thresholds. Aggregate promotion requires an explicit policy selection.
  • Adopt longprobe_report instead of private pytest config assignments; old named-decorator/rank-delta changelog claims are not implemented interfaces.
  • See v0.2.0 release notes for format, exit-code, fixture, and baseline changes. Hosted CI/publication remain pending.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Runtime version now derives from installed package metadata; base startup keeps optional SDKs lazy and missing SDK calls give installation guidance.
  • Invalid CLI configuration fails explicitly. Strict shapes, scalar types/ranges, and active environment credentials are validated before service calls; deliberate Python default configuration remains supported.
  • Empty evaluations fail across the scorer, Python facade, and CLI; failed reruns invalidate older reports for baseline saving.
  • Golden writes validate content and use same-directory atomic replacement, preserving existing data on ordinary preparation/write failures.
  • Auto-capture validates existing goldens before generation and never resets an unreadable or invalid set. Initialization preserves files unless forced.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Explicit generate --output PATH --overwrite for question-list replacement; incompatible output/auto-capture flags fail preflight.
  • Controlled HTTP workflow and failure-injection regression tests across supported Python versions.
  • Local HTTP quick-start fixture, accurate configuration examples, and recovery/known-limitations documentation.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Minimum Python version is now 3.11; Python 3.10 support and its CI job have been removed.
  • Empty selections and invalid settings that previously passed or fell back to defaults now fail.
  • Use an installed editable checkout for development; the runtime version requires distribution metadata.
  • No baseline database/schema migration. Embedding integration, baseline-policy unification, default pytest fixture repair, and general JSON-output cleanup remain deferred.
Historical development entry. Evaluation, baseline, pytest, and CI consistency was completed locally in the v0.2.0 candidate; hosted acceptance remains pending.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Draft vs. Approved Status Schema: Added status field (draft / approved) to GoldenQuestion. Auto-captured questions start in draft state so unvetted questions do not pollute regression suites.
  • Interactive TUI Editor (longprobe edit): Terminal editor using Rich to browse, filter, edit, and approve draft golden questions into trusted ground truth.
  • Pytest Plugin (pytest-longprobe): Early pytest integration. For v0.2.0 use the longprobe_report fixture; there is no supported @longprobe_check decorator.
  • Strict Baseline Quality Gating (longprobe baseline save): Prevents saving low-recall or degraded probe reports as trusted baselines (--threshold), evaluating strictly on approved questions.
  • Two-Baseline Comparison (longprobe diff <a <b>): Compare any two historical snapshot baselines side-by-side with --threshold quality verification.
  • Diagnostic Summaries (longprobe explain): Human-readable missing-evidence analysis. Rank deltas and distance drops are not implemented.
  • CLI --include-drafts Option: Flag on check and live diff to evaluate draft questions on demand.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
(For maintainers)

  1. Update CHANGELOG.md, set the version in pyproject.toml, and regenerate any changed demo GIFs.
  2. Commit the source changes and updated assets/*.gif files. The checkout README uses public GIF links from the configured repository’s main branch. Push changed assets there so previews show the latest published recordings.
  3. Push the release commit and matching v<version> tag to the public image repository configured in [tool.hatch.metadata.hooks.custom]. It currently points to Abdullahbinmushtaq/LongProbe; change image-base-url if another repository will host release images.
  4. Build with uv build. The metadata hook pins public or local GIF links to public URLs under the matching version tag in the wheel and source-distribution descriptions. It does not edit README.md or upload images.
  5. Run uv run python examples/verify_pypi_readme.py to check both distribution descriptions and confirm that package builds preserve the checkout README.
  6. Run uv run python examples/verify_pypi_readme.py --check-public before uploading to PyPI. This downloads the tagged public images and checks that they match your local release assets. The tag workflow runs this check before creating its GitHub release. A version change or PyPI upload alone does not publish GitHub assets. The existing tag workflow builds the package and creates a GitHub release; it does not upload to PyPI.

For example, package version 0.2.0 produces image URLs such as:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Abdullahbinmushtaq/LongProbe/v0.2.0/assets/01-complete-workflow.gif

Each release uses its own tagged assets, so later GIF changes on main do not change older PyPI descriptions. After changing the package version, build new distributions; uploading an older wheel will retain its older description.

docs.title: Complete Workflow
docs.text: Follow a retrieval change from reviewed golden questions to a saved baseline and a detected regression. This demonstration shows which question failed, what evidence disappeared, and why the quality check failed.

docs.title: Demo
docs.text: The dashboard uses animated progress panels, color-coded results, and a before-and-after comparison. It displays no Python source code. The GIF plays at twice the original recording speed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The demo tests three questions about refund policy, payment terms, and encryption. All three initially pass. After the sample retriever stops returning refund evidence, LongProbe detects one regression while the other two questions continue to pass.

It uses fixed sample documents and an in-memory retriever to exercise real LongProbe evaluation, comparison, and SQLite baseline promotion. No external API, vector database, embedding model, or credentials are needed. The sample is a retrieval regression demonstration; it does not evaluate generated answers or establish overall deployment readiness.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How draft questions become reviewed, approved test cases.
  • How recall percentages relate to required evidence.
  • When a report is eligible to become a trusted baseline.
  • How to select a reference explicitly and identify lost evidence.
  • Why a failed check should leave the trusted reference unchanged.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Golden Questions
docs.text:
Prepare three candidate questions with expected evidence and draft status. Drafts are excluded from ordinary checks until approved.

In your own project, write candidates manually or use capture or generate --auto-capture. Retrieved evidence is a candidate requirement: the retriever may already be returning incomplete or incorrect results.

docs.title: 2. Review and Approve Evidence
docs.text:
Check each question and required evidence item against its source document before changing its status to approved.

The recording displays the sample source evidence and illustrates approval using fixed, pre-reviewed fixtures. It does not perform human review or provide a separate approval system. In a real project, a person makes that review decision.

docs.title: 3. Run the Initial Evaluation
docs.text:
Evaluate the approved questions using an 85% recall threshold. The dashboard shows each question's recall, evidence found / required, and PASS/FAIL result.

All three sample questions initially find their required evidence. Overall recall and pass rate are both 100%.

docs.title: 4. Save a Trusted Baseline
docs.text:
Explicitly save the eligible report as production-v1. Under the default all_questions promotion policy, every evaluated approved question must pass. A good average cannot compensate for a failing question.

A passing check does not save a reference automatically. Python promotion reuses the retained evaluation snapshot; the CLI baseline save command performs a fresh evaluation.

docs.title: 5. Simulate a Retrieval Change
docs.text:
Remove refund evidence from the sample retriever while keeping the reviewed golden requirements unchanged.

This illustrates a failure that could follow an index update, document removal, or change to your retrieval pipeline. Keeping the requirements unchanged allows LongProbe to compare the same expectations before and after the change.

docs.title: 6. Detect and Explain the Regression
docs.text:
Evaluate again with production-v1 explicitly selected. The reports have compatible evaluation contracts, so LongProbe can identify the lost refund evidence and report a regression.

The final dashboard shows one failed question, one regression, zero improvements, and a failed quality verdict. The trusted baseline remains unchanged for investigation and recovery.

docs.title: Before-and-After Results
docs.text:
Metric Initial evaluation After refund evidence is removed Overall recall 100.0% 66.7% Pass rate 100.0% 66.7% Passing questions 3 of 3 2 of 3 Failing questions 0 1 Quality verdict PASS FAIL Historical comparison No reference exists yet Compatible with production-v1 Regressions / improvements Not applicable 1 / 0

Each sample question requires one evidence item:

Result Recall Evidence found / required Status Required evidence returned 100.0% 1 / 1 PASS Required evidence missing 0.0% 0 / 1 FAIL

Recall measures required evidence found. A retriever's similarity score is a different measurement and is not a correctness percentage. This synthetic demo does not display similarity scores.

docs.title: Run Locally
docs.text:
From the repository root containing pyproject.toml:

make setup-demos
demos/.recording_venv/bin/python demo_run/complete_workflow.py

For a run without presentation pauses:

demos/.recording_venv/bin/python demo_run/complete_workflow.py --no-delay

Setup requires Python 3.11 or newer and may download package dependencies. Once installed, the scenario runs without external services. It creates temporary golden, configuration, and baseline files, then removes them afterward.

The script verifies that the deliberate regression is detected and exits successfully when the demonstration behaves as expected. Its successful exit does not mean the second retrieval evaluation passed. To regenerate the GIFs, follow demos/README.md.

docs.title: Python API Example
docs.text:
For your application, supply its configured retriever adapter, reviewed golden suite, and scoring configuration. The example assumes those files and the adapter object already exist; set scoring.recall_threshold: 0.85 in longprobe.yaml to match the demo.

from longprobe import LongProbe

probe = LongProbe(
    adapter=adapter,
    goldens_path="goldens.yaml",
    config_path="longprobe.yaml",
)

# Evaluate the reviewed suite and explicitly promote an eligible reference.
report = probe.run()
assert report.quality["passed"], report.quality["reasons"]
probe.save_baseline(label="production-v1")

# After changing your application's retrieval pipeline:
report2 = probe.run(baseline_label="production-v1")
diff = report2.comparison
print(f"Compatible: {diff['compatible']}")
print(f"Regressions: {len(diff['regressions'])}")
print(f"Improvements: {len(diff['improvements'])}")
assert report2.quality["passed"], report2.quality["reasons"]

The final assertion fails for the deliberate missing-evidence scenario. It also catches individual question failures and incompatible comparisons. The recording shows that verdict through its dashboard without displaying code or a traceback.

docs.title: CLI Workflow for Your Application
docs.text:
Configure a working application retriever in longprobe.yaml before using these commands. This workflow operates on your application's data, rather than the recording's temporary fixtures.

# Capture a candidate question and evidence as a draft.
longprobe capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto

# Review the question and source evidence before approving it.
longprobe edit

# Inspect approved-question quality before establishing a reference.
longprobe check --no-compare
longprobe baseline save --label production-v1

# After changing your application's retrieval pipeline:
longprobe check --baseline production-v1

Inspect required evidence in YAML when needed; the editor does not expose every field. longprobe diff --baseline production-v1 is another way to run a live comparison. Each live command performs its own evaluation.

Intentional changes to question coverage or evaluation contracts can make strict comparison incompatible. Review those changes and explicitly establish a new reference when appropriate; do not replace expected evidence simply to make a failing check pass.

docs.title: Detect retrieval regressions
docs.text: The v0.2.0 dashboard scenario explicitly selects a baseline and displays compatibility, regression/improvement counts, lost evidence, and the shared quality verdict. A retrieval check does not establish overall deployment readiness.

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
From the repository root:

make setup-demos
demos/.recording_venv/bin/python demo_run/detect_regressions.py

The deterministic sample retriever starts with all three reviewed cases passing. The script saves an eligible reference, removes refund evidence, and evaluates again. It shows one regression, zero improvements, compatible contracts, and failed quality. Temporary files are removed afterward; no external database or embedding model is required.

docs.title: Python workflow
docs.text:
# probe is configured with your adapter and reviewed golden suite.
report = probe.run()
probe.save_baseline(label="production-v1")

# After an application retrieval change:
report2 = probe.run(baseline_label="production-v1")
diff = report2.comparison
print(f"Compatible: {diff['compatible']}")
print(f"Regressions: {len(diff['regressions'])}")
print(f"Improvements: {len(diff['improvements'])}")
assert report2.quality["passed"], report2.quality["reasons"]

The assertion fails if a selected question fails, evidence regresses, or a comparison is incompatible. Zero regressions alone is insufficient to establish passing quality. Missing explicit references fail before retrieval.

docs.title: CLI equivalent
docs.text:
With a working application retriever and reviewed golden questions:

longprobe baseline save --label production-v1
longprobe baseline list
longprobe check --baseline production-v1
longprobe diff --baseline production-v1

The last two commands are alternatives for a live comparison; each performs its own evaluation. A check never replaces the saved reference automatically. Changed coverage or evaluation contracts require review before intentionally establishing a new reference.

See baseline management and the CLI reference. Regenerate the GIF with make demos using the prerequisites in demos/README.md.

docs.title: Monitor RAG quality
docs.text:
The v0.2.0 dashboard shows one evaluation with per-question recall, required evidence found, pass/fail results, and the shared quality verdict. It also shows that no historical comparison occurred when a baseline is absent. Progress panels and result tables are displayed without source code.

Evidence is displayed as found / required, alongside recall percentage and PASS/FAIL. For example, 0 / 1 means zero of one required items was retrieved, giving 0% recall. Similarity scores are not correctness percentages and are not displayed by this synthetic demonstration.

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
From the repository root:

make setup-demos
demos/.recording_venv/bin/python demo_run/monitor_rag_quality.py

The script uses three reviewed sample cases, an 85% threshold, and a deterministic in-memory adapter. Refund evidence is deliberately omitted: two questions pass and one fails. Overall recall and pass rate are 66.7%, and the quality summary identifies the missing evidence. This is an expected demonstration failure; the script verifies it and exits successfully. It runs without an external service or optional vector SDK. Temporary files are removed after each run. Add --no-delay for immediate output.

docs.title: Inspect the verdict
docs.text:
report = probe.run()
print(f"Overall recall: {report.overall_recall:.1%}")
print(f"Pass rate: {report.pass_rate:.1%}")
print(report.baseline_identity)
assert report.quality["passed"], report.quality["reasons"]

A strong average can hide a failed question. Use the shared quality verdict to enforce each selected question's effective threshold and any available comparison. Passing does not automatically approve questions or save a baseline.

The fixture demonstrates evaluation behavior rather than live production monitoring. To evaluate your own application, supply its retriever and reviewed goldens. See the Python guide and pytest integration.

    url: http://localhost:8000/api/retrieve
    method: POST
    body_template: '{"query": "{question}", "top_k": {top_k}}'
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer ${API_TOKEN}
    response_mapping:
      results_path: data.chunks
      id_field: chunk_id
      text_field: content
      score_field: similarity
    timeout: 30
scoring:
  recall_threshold: 0.8
  fail_on_regression: true
  # Optional; replace with an ID in your full golden set:
  # question_thresholds:
  #   refund-policy: 1.0
baseline:
  db_path: .longprobe/baselines.db
  auto_compare: true
  quality_gate: all_questions

Remove the Authorization header when your local endpoint does not require authentication. HTTP settings live under retriever.http. Chroma/Pinecone/Qdrant connection fields live directly under retriever:

retriever:
  type: chroma
  collection: documents
  persist_directory: ./chroma_db

Pinecone uses index_name, api_key, and namespace. Qdrant uses collection, host, port, and optional api_key. Their normal text-question flow is not connected to query embeddings in this release; use a properly configured application HTTP endpoint or custom Python adapter until that integration is implemented. Framework retrievers require the Python API.

docs.title: Strict loading and accepted values
docs.text:
CLI commands that accept a configuration path require that selected file to exist and be valid. Invalid files never silently become default settings. init, edit, and help need no retriever configuration. Baseline list/delete use their existing --db-path option rather than reading longprobe.yaml.

Python callers supplying an adapter may omit the conventional longprobe.yaml; documented defaults are then used. ./longprobe.yaml has the same behavior. Missing custom/absolute selected paths raise FileNotFoundError. Any existing invalid selected file fails.

  • Supplied sections and nested HTTP settings must be mappings.
  • Omitted optional fields keep defaults; explicit invalid or null values fail.
  • Integer fields accept integers or integer strings; booleans and fractional values are invalid.
  • Floats must be finite. Recall threshold must be between 0 and 1.
  • Ports must be 1–65535, dimensions nonnegative, and timeouts/batch sizes/generation counts/token limits positive.
  • Booleans accept YAML booleans or case-insensitive strings true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off.
  • Provider-specific extra mappings are preserved; this release does not redesign unknown-key handling.

Validation errors identify fields without printing their values. Correct misspelled or incorrectly nested known settings; extra fields are not automatically used by every CLI adapter.

docs.title: Environment variables and active providers
docs.text:
${VARIABLE} values are expanded recursively. Unresolved placeholders in fields used by the current operation fail before its service calls. Unused generator/embedder credential placeholders do not block unrelated retrieval checks. Supplied typed numeric/structure settings are still validated even in inactive sections.

Generator configuration example:

generator:
  provider: ollama
  model: your-installed-model
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
  num_questions: 20
  temperature: 0.7
  max_tokens: 4096

Cloud generation may use generator.api_key or the provider environment variable, such as OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or GEMINI_API_KEY. Changing a generator model affects generated questions, not checks against existing goldens. Auto-capture validates both generator and retriever settings before generation. Local Chroma, unauthenticated Qdrant, and Ollama do not require unrelated cloud credentials.

docs.title: Scoring and baselines
docs.text:
recall_threshold controls the global per-question threshold. Invocation overrides supersede it, while explicit question_thresholds take precedence for their IDs. Values must be finite numbers in [0, 1]; unknown IDs fail against the full loaded suite, even when selection later filters questions.

baseline.quality_gate defaults to all_questions for both CLI and Python promotion. aggregate is an explicit alternative that permits individual failures if the mean meets the global threshold. Regular evaluation still reports every failed question.

fail_on_regression: true makes check fail for question failures or lost required evidence, including equal-recall evidence swaps. Setting it to false only relaxes completed quality failures; configuration, empty suites, incompatible comparisons, and execution failures remain nonzero. It never bypasses baseline promotion policy.

baseline.db_path selects SQLite storage. auto_compare uses literal latest when present. Explicit --baseline labels are required; --no-compare skips comparison. CI restores its database explicitly when configured. New report JSON metadata does not require an SQL table migration, but legacy references must be re-established before strict comparison. See baseline management.

docs.title: Embedding and matching limitations
docs.text:
The standalone QueryEmbedder utility supports provider/model/dimensions/batch-size settings, but normal check and LongProbe.run() do not invoke it. Local test mode produces zero vectors, not useful semantic embeddings. Changing only embedder.model does not change normal retrieval.

match_mode: semantic uses word-frequency cosine similarity. Its threshold belongs to each golden question and does not use QueryEmbedder.

docs.title: Safe files
docs.text:
Golden saves, initialized configuration files, and generated question exports use a same-directory temporary file, flush, and atomic replacement. Existing restrictions are preserved; read-only or symbolic-link replacement targets are rejected. Recoverable failures preserve original destination bytes. The guarantee is per file for a single writer, not a multi-file transaction or concurrent-write solution.

init preserves existing files unless --force is specified. Auto-capture always requires a valid existing golden file and merges new drafts. Question-list export requires --overwrite to replace an existing --output file. Back up important files before upgrading or making deliberate replacements.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: LongProbe tests whether your retriever still returns expected evidence for a fixed set of questions. It does not automatically inspect every live user query.

docs.title: 1. Install and initialize
docs.text:
pip install longprobe
longprobe init

Initialization creates two example files and a baseline directory:

  • goldens.yaml: questions and required evidence.
  • longprobe.yaml: retrieval connection, scoring, and baseline settings.
  • .longprobe/: local baseline storage.

The file content comes from GOLDENS_TEMPLATE and CONFIG_TEMPLATE strings in CLI source. init does not read documents, embeddings, or a database. Existing files are preserved unless you explicitly run longprobe init --force.

docs.title: 2. Configure a retriever
docs.text:
You need an existing retrieval endpoint or supported store. For a synthetic local example, run this command from a source checkout in another terminal:

python examples/http_retriever.py

This development fixture returns a known refund-policy chunk; it is not a production retrieval service. Configure longprobe.yaml:

retriever:
  type: http
  http:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve
    method: POST
    response_mapping:
      results_path: data.chunks
      id_field: chunk_id
      text_field: content
      score_field: similarity

scoring:
  recall_threshold: 0.8
  fail_on_regression: true

baseline:
  db_path: .longprobe/baselines.db
  auto_compare: true

For Chroma, install longprobe[chroma] and configure collection and persist_directory directly under retriever, not under a nested chroma section. The application/store handles its existing embedding model; the embedder configuration is not connected to the normal check path in this release.

docs.title: 3. Define verified golden questions
docs.text:
Replace the sample cases in goldens.yaml with requirements you have verified:

name: refund-policy
version: "1.0"
questions:
  - id: refund_policy
    question: What is the refund policy?
    required_chunks:
      - Refunds are allowed within 30 days.
    match_mode: text
    top_k: 5
    status: approved
    tags: [policy, critical]

Alternatively, capture a question through your configured retriever:

longprobe capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto
longprobe edit

Automatic capture saves drafts. In the editor, review the evidence in YAML as necessary, approve the intended drafts, and save. Interactive capture lets you select evidence and saves approved questions. Do not assume current retrieval output is independently correct ground truth.

For document-based generation, install longprobe[generate], configure your generator provider/model and credentials, then run:

longprobe generate ./documents --num-questions 20 --auto-capture
longprobe edit

PDF/Word extraction depends on installed parsing capabilities. Generating questions without --auto-capture produces a question list rather than a complete evaluable golden set. A fixed question count does not guarantee full document coverage; add reviewed cases for important topics and real retrieval failures. LongProbe checks selected golden questions, not arbitrary live user queries. The terminal editor currently edits question text, status, and mode; use YAML to review/change required evidence.

docs.title: 4. Check and save a baseline
docs.text:
longprobe check
longprobe baseline save --label latest

Every approved question is sent to the retriever. LongProbe matches the returned evidence, calculates recall, and applies the passing threshold. With fail_on_regression: true, a below-threshold question or detected baseline regression makes check fail.

latest is a literal baseline label. Saving another label does not update it. Both CLI and Python baseline promotion default to every evaluated question passing. Saving is explicit and never edits golden questions. Legacy references remain readable but need a reviewed new evaluation before strict comparison; see baseline management.

After changing your retrieval pipeline:

longprobe check
longprobe diff --baseline latest

docs.title: 5. Recover from input failures
docs.text:
Failure Action Missing CLI configuration Run init and configure it, or pass --config PATH Invalid YAML or value Correct the reported field/syntax; LongProbe will not silently use defaults Unresolved active credential Set the named environment variable or fix the active provider setting No matching/approved questions Correct tags, add questions, or review and approve drafts Invalid existing goldens during generation Repair the file or choose a new --goldens PATH; trusted data is not reset Existing question-list export Choose a new output path or explicitly use --output PATH --overwrite

Empty suites may be created/edited, but cannot pass evaluation. --include-drafts includes actual drafts, not an empty-suite bypass.

docs.title: Other entry points
docs.text:
longprobe check --output github
longprobe check --tag critical
longprobe watch

Watch polls the golden file and runs after a change; it does not initially run or watch configuration/remote index changes. Configuration edits take effect the next time a check is invoked.

See configuration, CLI reference, and v0.2.0 migration notes for limits and compatibility changes.

docs.title: Baseline management
docs.text: A baseline is an explicitly saved retrieval report used as the reference for later checks. It lives in the SQLite database selected by baseline.db_path, normally .longprobe/baselines.db.

docs.title: Save a trusted reference
docs.text:
longprobe check --no-compare
longprobe baseline save --label latest

baseline save performs a fresh evaluation of approved questions. By default every evaluated question must meet its effective recall threshold. A strong average cannot hide an individual failure. Empty selections and drafts cannot be promoted. A rejected promotion leaves the existing labeled reference intact.

The first command is optional inspection; its result is not silently reused by the second. Neither command edits goldens.yaml. Review any question or required-evidence changes against the source documents before approving them.

A passing check never replaces a baseline automatically. Saving an existing label explicitly replaces that label's report. Saving release-a does not update latest: latest is a literal name, not a newest-report lookup.

docs.title: Policy and threshold overrides
docs.text:
scoring:
  recall_threshold: 0.8
  question_thresholds:
    cancellation-policy: 1.0
baseline:
  quality_gate: all_questions

An invocation-level --threshold overrides the configured global threshold. Explicit per-question thresholds take precedence over that global override. Override IDs are validated against the complete loaded suite, so a typo fails while a valid override for an excluded question is allowed.

For an intentional average-based baseline policy:

baseline:
  quality_gate: aggregate

This explicit alternative permits individual failures when overall recall meets the effective global threshold. The report records that choice and retains individual failure details. It only changes baseline eligibility; regular checks still assess every selected question and regressions.

fail_on_regression: false does not disable baseline promotion gates, configuration validation, empty-selection rejection, or comparison compatibility checks.

docs.title: Select the reference
docs.text:
longprobe check --baseline release-a
longprobe diff --baseline release-a
longprobe diff release-a release-b
longprobe check --no-compare
longprobe baseline list --db-path .longprobe/baselines.db

An explicit missing label fails before retrieval. The default automatic comparison looks for optional latest; if it does not exist, quality can still be assessed, but the report says no historical comparison occurred. --no-compare skips the configured comparison; it cannot be combined with an explicit --baseline.

The report includes requested/resolved label, reference timestamp, and comparison status. Stored diff A B treats A as the reference and B as the target, without running retrieval.

docs.title: Understand differences and compatibility
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 reports carry effective matching, retrieval-limit, threshold, question, and evidence contracts. A strict comparison requires the same evaluated question coverage, suite name/version, and contracts. Reordering questions or required evidence does not make otherwise identical reports incompatible.

Comparisons surface added/removed question IDs, changed contract fields, and lost/gained required evidence. Losing previously found required evidence is a regression even if another requirement is found and total recall stays the same.

Changed coverage or contracts produce an incompatible outcome instead of a clean regression verdict. Raw scores remain available, but a like-for-like overall delta is unavailable. Review intentional changes, then explicitly establish a new reference if appropriate.

docs.title: Upgrade existing references
docs.text:
Unversioned v0.1.x rows remain readable/listable; adoption does not rewrite the database. Missing historical settings cannot be inferred safely, so strict comparisons against those rows are marked unverified and exit unsuccessfully.

  1. Close baseline writers and back up your database.
  2. Review the current approved questions, evidence, and settings.
  3. Inspect a fresh evaluation with longprobe check --no-compare.
  4. Explicitly save a new reference with longprobe baseline save --label latest when eligible.
  5. Retain the old backup or historical labels as needed.

A metadata-free old reference does not prevent independent baseline saving. No SQL table migration is required; new metadata is stored in report JSON. An older executable replacing a label may discard metadata it does not understand, so preserve backups before downgrading.

docs.title: Python promotion
docs.text:
report = probe.run()
probe.save_baseline(label="release-a")

The Python facade applies the same policy. It saves a retained evaluation snapshot: modifying the returned report or configuration afterward does not weaken that candidate. Run again to adopt new settings. Failed reruns invalidate prior candidates. A passing candidate can be explicitly promoted even when its comparison with an older incompatible reference is unavailable.

BaselineStore.save() is low-level storage, not a quality certification operation. Use the facade or CLI to promote trusted baselines.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Use longprobe COMMAND --help for implemented options. Default paths are goldens.yaml and longprobe.yaml.

Command Purpose init Create example files, preserving existing files unless --force check Evaluate selected questions with shared scoring/comparison rules capture Query supplied questions and select evidence; --auto creates drafts generate PATH Generate questions from documents; auto-capture creates draft cases edit Review status, question text/mode, approve drafts, and save baseline save Fresh approved-only evaluation and explicit policy-gated promotion baseline list List snapshots at --db-path baseline delete --label LABEL Confirm deletion of a snapshot at --db-path diff --baseline LABEL Compare a live run with an explicit reference diff LABEL_A LABEL_B Compare stored target B against reference A report REPORT_PATH Render saved JSON without configuration or retrieval explain QUESTION_ID Rerun evaluation and explain missing evidence watch Poll the golden file and rerun after changes

docs.title: Evaluation and output
docs.text:
longprobe check --goldens tests/goldens.yaml --config longprobe.yaml
longprobe check --threshold 0.9 --top-k 10
longprobe check --tag critical --tag billing
longprobe check --include-drafts
longprobe check --baseline release-a
longprobe check --no-compare
longprobe check --output json > result.json
longprobe report result.json --output github
longprobe baseline save --label latest --output json

Multiple tags require all specified tags. Empty suites and empty selections fail. Drafts are excluded by default and cannot be promoted. Global threshold overrides do not override explicit per-question settings.

check --baseline LABEL requires the label to exist. Optional automatic latest absence is visible in the report; no historical safety is implied. --no-compare deliberately disables comparison and cannot be combined with --baseline.

docs.title: JSON and exit codes
docs.text:
check, diff, baseline save, and report support table, json, and github output. Parsed JSON-mode invocations emit one complete JSON object on stdout, including handled command errors. Notices and diagnostics go to stderr.

Success/evaluation payloads include existing aggregate/result fields, schema_version, recorded contracts/policy, quality, baseline_identity, comparison, and a status. diff remains an alias for the comparison object for automation compatibility. Error envelopes contain schema_version, status: error, and error.code/error.message.

Code Meaning 0 Successful operation, or an explicitly nonblocking completed quality failure 1 Completed evaluation/comparison or baseline quality failure 2 Invalid input/setup, empty selection, missing explicit reference, or incompatible comparison 3 Operational or unexpected execution failure

A failed quality decision stays recorded as failed even when scoring.fail_on_regression: false allows a check to exit 0. That setting does not relax setup/execution failures or incompatible comparisons. Explicit diff gates quality; baseline promotion always applies its own policy.

Parser-level usage errors that prevent establishing a valid invocation use normal CLI stderr and code 2, without promising a JSON object. Watch and interactive authoring remain human-oriented. report renders completed data and does not re-enforce the saved quality verdict; malformed input still fails.

docs.title: Authoring
docs.text:
longprobe capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto
longprobe capture --questions-file questions.txt --match-mode id
longprobe generate ./documents --num-questions 20 --auto-capture
longprobe edit

Install generation dependencies and configure the provider/model before generation. Review required evidence in YAML; the editor does not expose every field. Automatic capture is candidate evidence, not independently verified truth. Generating questions does not guarantee complete document coverage.

Question-list export is separate:

longprobe generate ./documents --output questions.yaml
longprobe generate ./documents --output questions.yaml --overwrite

--overwrite requires --output, and output mode cannot be combined with --auto-capture. Invalid existing golden files fail preflight and are never silently reset.

docs.title: Baselines and watch
docs.text:
Saving another label does not update literal latest. New reports enforce contract compatibility; see baseline management for old reference migration and intentional rebaselining.

Watch runs after golden-file changes, not on startup or configuration/remote index changes. Failed iterations are reported and watching continues. Explain lists missing evidence and retrieved IDs; it does not calculate rank or distance deltas.

docs.title: Golden questions
docs.text: A golden suite is a reviewed set of example questions and the evidence your retriever must return. It tests retrieval after documents have been indexed and before answer generation. It does not judge the final LLM answer.

docs.title: File structure
docs.text:
The default filename is goldens.yaml; golden.yaml also works when selected with --goldens golden.yaml.

name: policy-retrieval
version: "1.0"
questions:
  - id: refund-policy
    question: "What is the refund policy?"
    status: draft
    match_mode: text
    required_chunks:
      - "30-day money-back guarantee"
      - "full refund within 30 days"
    top_k: 5
    tags: [policy, critical]

required_chunks contains stable chunk IDs in id mode or evidence text in text/semantic modes. top_k sets the requested result limit. Tags help select cases. Use explicit status: draft for unreviewed cases: omitted status defaults to approved for backward compatibility.

docs.title: Create and review the suite
docs.text:
1. Prepare documents, chunk them, and build your application's retrieval index.
  2. Write representative questions manually, or generate candidates from documents using a configured generation provider.
  3. Write required evidence from verified sources, or capture candidate results from the configured retriever.
  4. Review each question and every requirement against its source document. Current retrieval output can itself be incomplete or wrong.
  5. Change verified cases from draft to approved, using longprobe edit or a reviewed YAML edit. The editor does not expose every evidence field; inspect YAML when necessary.
  6. Run checks and explicitly save an eligible baseline after review.
longprobe generate ./documents --num-questions 20 --auto-capture
longprobe edit
longprobe check --no-compare
longprobe baseline save --label latest

Generation needs its optional dependencies and configured provider. Ordinary generate produces questions; --auto-capture additionally retrieves candidate evidence and saves draft cases. Alternatively, capture --question "What is the refund policy?" --auto creates a draft from a supplied question. init copies examples; it does not read your documents or establish correct evidence.

docs.title: Human review and approval
docs.text:
Stage Human action Generate questions or auto-capture evidence Review candidates afterward; automatic output is not trusted ground truth Promote draft to approved Verify relevance, source correctness, and required evidence before changing status Run approved questions Runs automatically in CLI, pytest, or CI; no interactive approval is required Save or replace a trusted baseline Explicitly promote an eligible report after reviewing changes Change documents, questions, evidence, or settings Review the intended change and establish a new reference when contracts become incompatible

These are explicit editing and promotion actions, not a separate enforced manager sign-off system. Passing checks never automatically rewrite approved evidence or replace a baseline. Drafts are excluded by default; check --include-drafts can inspect them, but draft-containing reports cannot become trusted baselines.

docs.title: Coverage and maintenance
docs.text:
A suite covers selected cases, not every possible document question. Start with critical facts, representative topics, and known failure cases. Add cases when documents or real query patterns expose a gap.

A live user question absent from the suite has no golden expected evidence, so LongProbe cannot automatically certify that question's retrieval correctness. Review it, add expected evidence, and approve the case to include it in future checks.

The file remains editable. Make deliberate, reviewable changes in version control; do not copy current retrieval output into approved requirements just to make a failed test pass. Changed coverage or evaluation contracts make strict baseline comparison incompatible. Inspect intentional changes with check --no-compare, then explicitly save a reviewed reference when eligible. See baseline management.

docs.title: Scoring example
docs.text:
If two required evidence items are specified and only one is found, recall is 1 / 2 = 50%. Passing depends on that question's effective threshold. An unchanged average does not hide lost required evidence when comparing compatible reports.

See match modes, configuration, and the CLI reference.

docs.title: Match Modes
docs.text: LongProbe supports three match modes for verifying retrieved chunks.

docs.title: ID Match
docs.text:
Exact string match on chunk/document IDs.

match_mode: "id"
required_chunks:
  - "doc_a_chunk_3"
  - "doc_b_chunk_7"

docs.title: Text Match
docs.text:
Case-insensitive substring matching.

match_mode: "text"
required_chunks:
  - "30-day money-back guarantee"

docs.title: Semantic Match
docs.text:
Word-frequency cosine similarity.

match_mode: "semantic"
semantic_threshold: 0.80
required_chunks:
  - "Only the CFO and CEO may authorize payments"

docs.title: Choosing a Match Mode
docs.text:
• ID: When you control chunk IDs
  • Text: For exact phrases
  • Semantic: When wording may vary

docs.title: Python interface
docs.text:
Use your existing retriever through an adapter. LongProbe tests retrieval evidence; it does not index documents or evaluate the generated answer.

from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainRetrieverAdapter

adapter = LangChainRetrieverAdapter(your_application_retriever)
probe = LongProbe(
    adapter=adapter,
    goldens_path="goldens.yaml",
    config_path="longprobe.yaml",
)
report = probe.run()
assert report.quality["passed"], report.quality["reasons"]

Replace your_application_retriever with the retriever already constructed by your application. HTTP and other supported adapters can be created through create_adapter_from_config(config); optional backend SDKs remain lazy.

docs.title: Evaluation and references
docs.text:
report = probe.run(top_k_override=10, tags=["critical"])
report = probe.run(baseline_label="release-a")
differences = probe.diff(baseline_label="release-a")

run() returns ProbeReport, including per-question results/contracts, aggregate scores, selected baseline identity, structured comparison, and the quality decision. Quality failure is returned as data; invalid input and failed execution raise exceptions. Explicit missing labels fail. The default automatic reference is optional latest.

To deliberately evaluate without the default comparison, set probe.config.baseline.auto_compare = False before running. An explicit baseline_label still requests that reference.

CLI and Python share evaluation and policy resolution. A global recall_threshold constructor override supersedes the configured global value; explicit scoring.question_thresholds still take precedence for their question IDs. Unknown override IDs fail before retrieval.

docs.title: Save a baseline
docs.text:
probe.run()
probe.save_baseline(label="latest")

Every evaluated question must pass under the default policy. Draft-containing reports cannot be promoted. The optional aggregate policy must be selected explicitly in configuration and is captured with the evaluation.

The facade retains a defensive snapshot after a completed run. Editing the returned report or changing settings afterward cannot weaken its promotion policy. A failed rerun clears the old candidate. Use another run() to evaluate changed settings, and catch BaselineQualityError from longprobe.core.policy if you need to handle a rejected promotion.

docs.title: Configuration and in-memory suites
docs.text:
You may supply golden_set=GoldenSet(...) instead of a golden YAML path. The facade applies approved-only selection by default; use include_drafts=True for analysis. Tag filtering requires all selected tags. Empty selections fail.

When you supply an adapter and the conventional longprobe.yaml is absent, documented Python defaults are supported. Explicit missing custom paths and existing invalid files fail. Unused built-in retriever credentials are not required for your supplied adapter.

docs.title: Reports and comparisons
docs.text:
New reports use schema version 2. Old unversioned reports remain readable but cannot establish strict compatibility when historical settings are missing. Changed requirements, retrieval limits, thresholds, suite identity, or selected question coverage are surfaced rather than silently compared as the same test.

probe.diff() returns the same comparison fields used by CLI output, including compatible, compatibility_reasons, coverage/contract/evidence changes, regressions, improvements, and a nullable overall_delta. Check compatibility before interpreting the delta.

See baseline management, pytest integration, and release migration notes.

docs.title: CI/CD integration
docs.text: LongProbe v0.2.0 evaluates once and derives JSON, GitHub annotations, and PR feedback from that saved report. Setup, incompatible comparisons, invalid reports, and execution failures always fail the workflow. You can explicitly make completed quality failures nonblocking.

docs.title: Call the reusable workflow
docs.text:
name: Retrieval regression check
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  retrieval:
    uses: ENDEVSOLS/LongProbe/.github/workflows/longprobe.yml@main
    with:
      python-version: "3.12"
      longprobe-version: "0.2.0"
      config-path: longprobe.yaml
      goldens-path: goldens.yaml
      fail-on-regression: true
    secrets:
      retriever-api-key: ${{ secrets.RAG_RETRIEVER_API_KEY }}

Use a reviewed release tag or commit when available instead of a moving branch. The requested package version must be published before this installation path can succeed. The workflow requires v0.2.0 or newer. An empty version input installs the available default and then checks compatibility.

install-extras is a separate input, for example chroma. HTTP retrieval is included in the base package; there is no http extra.

If required, reference the optional credential in your configuration:

retriever:
  type: http
  http:
    url: https://your-application.example/retrieve
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${LONGPROBE_RETRIEVER_API_KEY}"

Replace the URL and configure the response mapping for your endpoint. Supply other application-specific authentication through your own wrapper workflow if needed. Never put secrets in golden files or report artifacts.

docs.title: Restore a trusted baseline
docs.text:
Fresh GitHub runners do not retain a previous job's SQLite file. Configure an artifact and source run explicitly:

with:
  longprobe-version: "0.2.0"
  baseline-artifact-name: longprobe-baseline
  baseline-run-id: "123456789"
  baseline-label: latest
  baseline-path: .longprobe/baselines.db

Replace the example run ID with the actual source run. The source must be a successful push, schedule, or workflow_dispatch run on the caller repository's default branch. The caller must allow artifact read permissions. A PR-produced report is not selected automatically as trusted ground truth.

The artifact must contain exactly one regular .db file from a closed standalone LongProbe SQLite database. Its requested label must exist, its contracts must match the selected approved suite/settings, and baseline-path must match baseline.db_path in configuration. Legacy metadata, missing artifacts/labels, journal sidecars, and incompatible suites fail setup; they are not treated as passing comparisons.

Without restoration inputs, the helper runs check --no-compare. The report explicitly says no historical comparison was requested. It does not silently use an unrelated checked-out database.

docs.title: Publish a baseline deliberately
docs.text:
After reviewing the golden set and deciding to establish a new reference:

longprobe baseline save --label latest

This command performs a fresh approved-only evaluation and enforces the selected baseline quality policy. A successful check does not update the reference automatically.

A maintainer-controlled workflow can retain that explicitly promoted reference:

- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
  with:
    name: longprobe-baseline
    path: .longprobe/baselines.db
    include-hidden-files: true
    if-no-files-found: error

Upload only the intended database. The hidden-file option is needed for a path under .longprobe; do not upload an entire configuration directory. See examples/ci_example/save-reviewed-baseline.yml in the repository for a manually invoked example.

docs.title: Reports and verdicts
docs.text:
The reusable workflow retains longprobe-result.json, longprobe-diagnostics.txt, and the derived longprobe-comment.md. It does not upload a new trusted baseline automatically.

The final verdict comes from the saved report and process outcome together. fail-on-regression: false only relaxes completed quality failures. It cannot hide invalid configuration, missing/incompatible references, invalid JSON, or a crashed command. A report's quality status remains failed even if the process is allowed to exit successfully.

Fork PRs receive annotations/artifacts without attempted write comments. A denied same-repository comment is reported separately; it does not change the evaluation result.

docs.title: Run the same workflow locally
docs.text:
python -m longprobe.ci run --config longprobe.yaml --goldens goldens.yaml
longprobe report longprobe-result.json --output github

The first command evaluates once. The second only renders existing data. Use --baseline LABEL with the helper for an explicitly prepared local reference, or --nonblocking to relax quality failures. GitHub artifact download and PR publication still require the hosted workflow.

docs.title: Migration and validation
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 adds strict report compatibility and per-question baseline gates. Re-establish a reviewed baseline when adopting an old metadata-free reference; do not invent missing historical settings. See release notes and baseline management.

Implementation references: artifact download inputs, artifact uploads and hidden files. Hosted execution must still be verified after the maintainer pushes the changes.

docs.title: LangChain integration
docs.text: Wrap your application's LangChain retriever with LangChainRetrieverAdapter. Install longprobe[langchain] and any provider-specific packages your application uses. For the unreleased v0.2.0 candidate, install the checkout as explained in installation.

docs.title: Connect an existing retriever
docs.text:
from longprobe import LongProbe
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainRetrieverAdapter

# application_retriever is your already configured LangChain retriever.
probe = LongProbe(
    adapter=LangChainRetrieverAdapter(application_retriever),
    goldens_path="goldens.yaml",
    config_path="longprobe.yaml",
)
report = probe.run()
assert report.quality["passed"], report.quality["reasons"]

The application supplies application_retriever; LongProbe does not construct your ingestion pipeline or configure its embeddings. Use a configuration file for scoring and baseline policy. A supplied adapter avoids connecting to an unused built-in backend.

The adapter calls invoke(query), with a fallback to get_relevant_documents(query). It maps page_content to text and copies metadata. IDs come from metadata["chunk_id"], then metadata["source"], then a positional doc_N fallback. Use stable, unique chunk_id values for ID matching. A document source shared by multiple chunks is not a unique chunk ID.

top_k truncates returned results; it does not increase the upstream retriever's configured result limit. Configure your application's retriever to return enough candidates.

docs.title: Baselines and pytest
docs.text:
After reviewing the golden evidence, explicitly save a passing candidate:

probe.save_baseline(label="production-v1")
report = probe.run(baseline_label="production-v1")
assert report.quality["passed"], report.quality["reasons"]

A good overall mean alone does not guarantee passing quality. The shared verdict includes individual failures, regressions, and incompatible comparisons. Promotion uses its recorded baseline policy.

For pytest, override the supported longprobe_adapter fixture to return LangChainRetrieverAdapter(application_retriever), then request longprobe_report or enable automatic enforcement. See pytest integration for session reuse and required configuration.

For a custom retrieval chain, subclass AbstractRetrieverAdapter and implement retrieve(query, top_k) returning dictionaries with id, text, score, and metadata. There is no built-in CustomAdapter class. See the Python guide and baseline management.

docs.title: Pytest integration
docs.text: The installed LongProbe package registers its pytest plugin automatically. Install pytest separately in your test environment. Tests can request a shared evaluation report or enable automatic quality enforcement.

docs.title: Evaluate once and inspect the report
docs.text:
Configure your retriever in longprobe.yaml and review the approved questions in goldens.yaml:

def test_retrieval(longprobe_report):
    assert longprobe_report.quality["passed"], longprobe_report.quality["reasons"]

pytest --longprobe-config tests/longprobe.yaml --longprobe-goldens tests/goldens.yaml

The selected configuration path is forwarded to the probe. The session-scoped longprobe_report fixture evaluates once per pytest process, even when several tests request it. The terminal summary uses that same report. You do not need to assign private attributes on pytest's configuration.

Without an assertion or enforcement option, the report fixture returns failed quality results for inspection; requesting a report alone does not automatically assert its quality. Invalid setup and failed execution remain test errors.

docs.title: Enforce quality automatically
docs.text:
pytest --longprobe-fail-threshold 0.85

This option activates the evaluation even when no user test requests longprobe_report. Every selected question must pass, and any detected regression or incompatible comparison fails the gate. Configured scoring.question_thresholds take precedence over the invocation's global threshold. A setting that makes CLI quality failures nonblocking does not disable explicit pytest enforcement.

Version 0.2.0 changes the old option's aggregate-oriented description: a good average cannot hide an individually failing question. Invalid thresholds and invalid requested configuration fail rather than skip tests. Pytest retains its own exit-code conventions.

Without requested LongProbe fixtures or the enforcement option, the plugin does not load configuration or call a retriever. If no tests are collected, normal pytest no-tests behavior applies.

docs.title: Use an application-owned retriever
docs.text:
Override the adapter fixture in conftest.py:

import pytest
from longprobe.adapters import LangChainRetrieverAdapter

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def longprobe_adapter():
    return LangChainRetrieverAdapter(build_application_retriever())

build_application_retriever() represents your application's setup function. A custom adapter does not require credentials for an unused built-in backend. Evaluation/scoring/baseline settings still come from the selected configuration.

docs.title: Fixtures and options
docs.text:
Fixture Purpose longprobe_report One completed session evaluation longprobe_probe Configured Python facade; manual run() calls deliberately evaluate again longprobe_adapter Default configured adapter or your override longprobe_config_path Selected configuration path longprobe_goldens_path Selected golden-set path longprobe_fail_threshold Optional invocation threshold longprobe_include_drafts Whether analysis includes drafts

Use --longprobe-include-drafts to analyze drafts explicitly. Draft-containing results cannot be promoted to a trusted baseline. Review candidate questions and evidence before approval.

docs.text: Status: implemented locally; package publication and hosted Actions acceptance are pending. No tag or push is performed by the implementation task. See the verification record for actual environments and limitations.

docs.title: Delivered behavior
docs.text: Area Change Evaluation CLI and Python coordinate selection, scoring, policy, and reference comparison through one module Baseline quality Default promotion requires every evaluated question to pass; explicit aggregate and per-question threshold settings are validated Comparison Added/removed questions, changed requirements/settings, and lost/gained required evidence are visible Compatibility Recorded matching/retrieval/threshold contracts determine strict comparability; incompatible suites have no like-for-like aggregate delta Baseline identity Requested/resolved labels, reference timestamp, and comparison status are recorded and displayed Pytest Configured default/custom adapters, session report reuse, and explicit automatic enforcement work without private user assignments Automation Parsed JSON invocations emit one stdout object; command failures have documented categories CI One evaluation supplies annotations/comments; configured trusted artifacts are validated/restored, version input is honored, and quality relaxation cannot hide setup errors

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Back up your SQLite baseline file with writers closed.
  2. Review goldens.yaml and approve only verified questions/evidence.
  3. Inspect threshold policy, including any per-question overrides.
  4. Run longprobe check --no-compare to inspect current quality independently.
  5. Explicitly save a reviewed eligible reference with longprobe baseline save --label latest.
  6. Update JSON consumers and pytest usage to the documented interfaces.
  7. Configure a successful trusted default-branch baseline run/artifact for reusable CI comparisons.

docs.title: Behavior changes
docs.text:
• CLI and Python baseline promotion now use the same default gate. An average above threshold does not compensate for a failed question. Select baseline.quality_gate: aggregate explicitly only when that is the intended policy.
  • Per-question thresholds override invocation/global thresholds. Unknown IDs fail against the full loaded suite.
  • Python retains a defensive candidate with its evaluation-time policy. Later mutation of the returned report or configuration does not weaken it; rerun to adopt new settings.
  • Removed/added evaluated questions and changed contracts make strict whole-suite comparison incompatible. Equal-recall evidence loss is a regression.
  • Existing unversioned reports load and list without rewriting, but missing historical settings make strict comparison unverified. Independent baseline saving remains available.
  • latest remains literal. Saving another label does not update it. Explicit missing references fail; optional default absence is visible.
  • check --baseline LABEL selects a required reference. check --no-compare skips comparison and cannot be combined with that explicit label.
  • JSON includes schema version 2, full result contracts, policy/quality, baseline identity, and comparison metadata. Existing aggregate keys and the diff alias remain available. A handled input/execution error uses a separate safe error envelope.
  • Exit codes are 0 for success/nonblocking quality, 1 for blocking quality, 2 for invalid/empty/incompatible setup, and 3 for execution failures. Parser-level usage errors retain ordinary stderr/code 2 behavior.
  • longprobe report PATH renders a validated saved report without retrieval. Rendering does not itself re-enforce the report's quality gate.
  • longprobe_report is the supported pytest fixture. --longprobe-fail-threshold now enforces selected questions and comparison quality rather than relying on an aggregate description and private config state.
  • Reusable workflow baseline restoration is explicit. Missing restoration inputs run unbaselined; configured invalid/missing artifacts fail. Comments can be skipped for restricted PR permissions without changing the verdict.

No SQL table migration is required. New report JSON fields are stored in existing rows only when explicitly saving/replacing a label. Old executables can discard metadata they do not understand if used to replace labels; preserve backups before downgrading.

docs.title: Unchanged scope and limitations
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer; the validated interpreter matrix remains 3.11 and 3.12. This release retains strict configuration, empty-evaluation rejection, stale-state invalidation, optional-SDK lazy imports, and safe golden-file writes.

Normal evaluation does not wire embedding conversion into vector-only Pinecone/Qdrant flows. Semantic matching remains word-frequency cosine similarity. Adapter error swallowing that predates this work is not redesigned; propagated retrieval failures are classified operationally. Explain does not calculate rank/score deltas, and watch still responds only to golden-file changes.

Golden suites test selected reviewed examples, not all possible questions or every live user query. Generated/captured evidence still needs human review. Baseline promotion and golden approval remain explicit; there is no new manager sign-off application.

The older changelog's named @longprobe_check and historical rank/distance explanation claims do not describe supported v0.2.0 interfaces. Use the documented report fixture and missing-evidence explanation behavior.

See CLI reference, baseline management, Python interface, pytest, and CI/CD.
